for_loop, misconceptions: 21 edges offered

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:for_loop->BracelessMultiStatementBody | wrong rule: Indenting several statements under an if or for makes them all part of its body, even without braces. | right rule: Without braces only the first statement belongs to the if/for; the rest run once, after it. | | err:for_loop->ForCommaSeparators | wrong rule: Writes for (int i = 0, i < n, i++). | right rule: The three parts of a for header are separated by semicolons; commas only separate several statements inside the init or the update part. | | err:for_loop->SemicolonAfterIfHeader | wrong rule: if (x > 0); System.out.println("positive"); prints only for positive x. | right rule: The ; ends the if with an empty statement, so the next line always runs. | | err:for_loop->SemicolonAfterLoopHeader | wrong rule: Puts a ; right after for (...) or while (...). | right rule: A ; right after the loop header is a null (empty) loop body, so the statements written after it are not repeated by the loop. | | err:for_loop->WrongIterationCount | wrong rule: Updates the loop counter so that the loop runs the wrong number of times. | right rule: The init, test and update together decide the number of passes; trace them to check the count. | | mis:for_loop->DoubleLoopIndexCount | wrong rule: for (double x = 0.0; x <= 1.0; x += 0.1) runs exactly 11 times. | right rule: Using a double as a for-loop index is legal but bad practice: the number of iterations depends on an equality test between double values, which may not give the result you expect. | | mis:for_loop->FalseLoopRepeatsNextCode | wrong rule: A loop is an iterative if-else: while the condition is true the body repeats, and when it is false the code after the loop repeats. | right rule: Only the body is repeated; once the condition is false the code after the loop runs once. | | mis:for_loop->ForInitRepeats | wrong rule: The initialization of a for loop runs again after a pass of the body. | right rule: The initialization runs exactly once, before the first condition test. | | mis:for_loop->ForIsConditional | wrong rule: The body of a for statement executes at most once. | right rule: The body of a for statement runs once for every pass on which the condition is true, which can be many times. | | mis:for_loop->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:for_loop->ForUpdateBeforeBody | wrong rule: The update part of a for header (e.g. i = i - 4) runs before the body on each pass, so the first pass already sees the updated value. | right rule: The update runs after the body, before the next condition test; the first pass uses the initial value. | | mis:for_loop->ForWhileNotInterchangeable | wrong rule: Some loops can only be written with for, others only with while. | right rule: Any for loop can be rewritten as a while loop and vice versa; for just packages init, test and update. | | mis:for_loop->IdiomOverridesCode | wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. | right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written. | | mis:for_loop->LoopCountIsStatementCount | wrong rule: The repeat count of a counted loop says how many of the body statements are executed. | right rule: The repeat count is how many times the whole body runs; every pass runs all body statements. | | mis:for_loop->LoopHeaderIsEquations | wrong rule: The initialization, condition and update of a for header are equations that all hold at the same time. | right rule: The three header parts are statements run at different moments: init once, then condition test, body, update, repeated. | | mis:for_loop->LoopImpliedByOneTest | wrong rule: Testing one case is enough; Java will repeat the test for the other values by itself. | right rule: A statement runs once each time control reaches it; repeating a test for many values needs a loop. | | mis:for_loop->LoopStepAlwaysOne | wrong rule: A loop variable always goes up or down by 1, whatever the update says (so i = i - 4 is read as i--). | right rule: The loop variable changes exactly as the update expression says (i += 2, i = i - 4, i *= 2, ...). | | mis:for_loop->MissingBraces | wrong rule: Omits braces around a single-statement body of if, for or while. | right rule: Braces are optional for a single-statement body, but using them anyway avoids bugs when statements are added later. | | mis:for_loop->ProgramEndsAfterLoop | wrong rule: When a loop finishes the program ends, so code after the loop never runs. | right rule: When the loop condition becomes false, control continues with the first statement after the loop. | | mis:for_loop->ReturnDoesNotExitLoop | wrong rule: A return inside a loop does not end the loop; it sets a value each pass (the last one is returned) or returns several values. | right rule: When return executes, the method ends at once, so the loop stops on that pass. | | mis:for_loop->SingleIterationInsteadOfLoop | wrong rule: A task that must be repeated is written once, without a loop, as if one pass were enough. | right rule: A step that must happen several times (or an unknown number of times) needs a loop such as while or for; code without a loop runs once. |

(here mixing in: "The body of a for statement executes at most once") | | lvl:for_loop@L1#0 | level L1 way names_the_element: The for statement is a loop that packages an initialization, a loop-continuation condition and an increment in its header around a body. | | lvl:for_loop@L1#1 | level L1 way states_the_rule: Syntax: for (; ; ) { }, with the three parts separated by semicolons; it is, with only a few exceptions, equivalent to ; while () { ; }. | | lvl:for_loop@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: Run the initializer once; the body applies its changes once; the update then changes the loop variable by its rule; the initializer changes state only once, before the first test. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#0 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The for header is exactly the three loop-control slots; the body runs after the test and before the update on each pass. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#1 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A for may be the body of another for: the inner for runs its complete set of passes for every single pass of the outer one. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#2 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) gives i each valid index 0..N-1 exactly once in increasing order, the standard way to process every array element. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#3 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A simulation runs a fixed number of trials with an outer for loop (for (int t = 0; t < T; t++)), each trial simulated inside the body. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#4 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: In a for loop, continue skips the rest of the body and transfers control directly to the increment, then the next test; this is one of the few places where the for/while equivalence fails. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#5 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A variable declared in the for header is in scope only in the header and the body, so it cannot be used after the loop. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#6 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A fencepost loop is a for loop that handles one item (the first or last) outside the loop so that separators come out n-1 times for n items. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#7 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A flag search loop is a for loop that sets a boolean flag when some pass finds the target and leaves it set afterwards; the flag must be declared before the loop. | | lvl:for_loop@L3#8 | level L3 way purpose_of_the_whole: Plan: counted loop / counter-controlled repetition - do the body a known number of times, with the loop variable as a stepper (index, term number, trial number). | | lvl:for_loop@L4#0 | level L4 way predict_a_change: Rewriting a for as the equivalent while (init before, update at the end of the body) keeps behaviour, except that continue then skips the update and the loop variable stays in scope after the loop. Changing the bound or the step changes the pass count predictably (< to <= adds one pass). | | lvl:for_loop@L4#1 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: The three parts of a for header are separated by semicolons; commas only separate several statements inside the init or the update. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Writing for (int i = 0, i < n, i++): the compiler parses the commas as more declarators in the init and reports a syntax error. | | lvl:for_loop@L4#2 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: A ; right after while (...) or for (...) is an empty statement that is the whole loop body; the block written next is not repeated. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: for (...); { body } runs the body once after the loop ends; while (cond); with a cond that the empty body cannot change hangs forever (infinite loop) when cond starts true. | | lvl:for_loop@L4#3 | level L4 way transfer_to_a_new_program: Use for when there is an initialization, an increment and a continuation test and the loop variable is not needed after the loop; use while when the loop variable is needed later or the number of passes depends on what happens in the body. | | lvl:for_loop@L4#4 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: A ; right after if (...) is an empty statement that forms the whole then branch; the following statement or block is no longer part of the if. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Any if (cond); followed by a statement or block: that statement runs for every input, whatever cond is (it compiles without error). | | lvl:for_loop@L4#5 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: The number of passes is fixed by the init, the test and the update together. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Wrong start value, < vs <=, a wrong step, or an extra update of the counter in the body (or outside the loop): the loop runs too few or too many passes (off by one, or skips values). | | lvl:for_loop@L4#6 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: Without braces, the body of an if, while or for is exactly one statement; indentation does not add statements to it. Kind: silent logic error. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: Reading i after for (int i = 0; ...) {...}: 'cannot find symbol'. |

loop_body, misconceptions: 12 edges offered

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:loop_body->BracelessMultiStatementBody | wrong rule: Indenting several statements under an if or for makes them all part of its body, even without braces. | right rule: Without braces only the first statement belongs to the if/for; the rest run once, after it. | | mis:loop_body->ComputerFillsInIntent | wrong rule: The computer fills in omitted steps or values that the programmer meant, e.g. REPEAT 4 [FORWARD 30] draws a square without a turn command. | right rule: The computer executes only what the code states; every needed step and value must be written. | | mis:loop_body->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:loop_body->IfInLoopUnchecked | wrong rule: An if inside a loop body runs its branch on every pass without testing its condition. | right rule: The if condition is tested again on every pass, with the current values, so the branch runs only on passes where it is true. | | mis:loop_body->LoopBodyAlwaysOnce | wrong rule: The loop body always runs at least once, even if the condition is false at the start. | right rule: A while or for body runs zero times when the condition is false at the start. | | mis:loop_body->LoopBodyStatementOutsideLoop | wrong rule: Some statements inside the braces of a loop body are not repeated; they run once, before or after the loop. | right rule: Every statement inside the loop braces is part of the body and runs on every pass. | | mis:loop_body->LoopCountIsStatementCount | wrong rule: The repeat count of a counted loop says how many of the body statements are executed. | right rule: The repeat count is how many times the whole body runs; every pass runs all body statements. | | mis:loop_body->LoopOutputSameEachPass | wrong rule: A loop prints the same thing on every pass; the changing loop variable does not affect what the body does. | right rule: The body uses the current value of the loop variable, so its output can differ on each pass. | | mis:loop_body->LoopRunsStatementsSeparately | wrong rule: A loop runs its first body statement all N times, then its second body statement all N times. | right rule: Each pass runs the whole body in order, so the body statements interleave: S1, S2, S1, S2, ... | | mis:loop_body->StateChangeIgnoredAcrossPasses | wrong rule: Values changed by one pass of a loop (other than the loop variable) do not affect later passes. | right rule: Each pass starts from the state left by the previous pass, so a change in one pass carries into the next ones. | | mis:loop_body->StatementAfterLoopInBody | wrong rule: A statement written after the loop is repeated with the loop body. | right rule: The body ends at the closing brace (or after its single statement); code after it runs once, after the loop ends. | | mis:loop_body->WhileStopsMidBody | wrong rule: The loop stops the moment the condition becomes false, even in the middle of the body. | right rule: The condition is tested only before each pass, so the whole body finishes before the loop can stop. |
